WHAT: Keyboard appearance detection uses two sources: (1) textDocumentProxy.keyboardAppearance for explicit app-set appearance, (2) traitCollection.userInterfaceStyle as fallback when app uses .default.

HOW:
```swift
func updateAppearance() {
    let appearance = textDocumentProxy.keyboardAppearance
    let isDark: Bool
    if appearance == .dark {
        isDark = true
    } else if appearance == .light {
        isDark = false
    } else {
        // .default — use system trait
        isDark = traitCollection.userInterfaceStyle == .dark
    }
    // apply isDark to key colors
}

override func traitCollectionDidChange(_ previous: UITraitCollection?) {
    super.traitCollectionDidChange(previous)
    updateAppearance()
}
```

WHY: Most apps use .default which means follow system. Without the traitCollection fallback, keyboard stays light even in system dark mode.

GOTCHA: Light-mode keyboard on a dark-background web page stays light — this is CORRECT and matches Apple keyboard behavior. The keyboard follows system mode, not app bg color.
